Chapter 8: Leading by Example—Inspiring Others Through Adversity.
As you get better at handling life’s challenges, there’s a natural next step that often calls out to you: leading others through tough times, too. But here’s the thing—real leadership in adversity isn’t about barking orders or trying to control everything. It’s about showing courage, living with integrity, and staying calm, even when the going gets rough.
Picture a leader in a crisis. Maybe it’s at home, at work, or even within a community. The way they act sets the tone for everyone else. If they keep their cool, focus on finding solutions, and treat everyone with respect, that sense of stability and hope becomes contagious. People start to believe they can get through anything, together.
So, what does it look like to actually lead by example? Here are a few habits worth keeping in mind:
First, communicate clearly and honestly about what’s going on and what might help. People appreciate straight talk, especially when things are uncertain.
Second, make decisions calmly and rationally—even when you’re under pressure. It’s not always easy, but showing that steady hand can make a world of difference.
And third, invite others to pitch in with their own ideas and solutions. When people feel like they’re part of the process, they care more about the outcome.
Let’s put this into a real-world scenario. Imagine a manager whose team is staring down the threat of layoffs. Instead of hiding behind closed doors, this manager acknowledges how tough things are, shares information openly, and rolls up their sleeves to work with the team on creative solutions. Even if the final outcome isn’t perfect, that openness and effort build trust, boost morale, and bring people closer together. The journey itself becomes a source of strength.
But leadership isn’t just about steering the ship through storms; it’s also about empowering others to face their own challenges. Maybe you’re mentoring a colleague through a tough assignment, supporting a friend after a loss, or standing up for what’s right when change is needed. These moments matter.
Here are a few reminders when you’re guiding others through adversity:
Model the attitudes and actions you hope to see in your team or community.
Encourage openness, support, and a sense of shared responsibility.
And don’t forget to celebrate progress—yes, even the small wins. Those little steps forward can mean everything.
When you lead with empathy and steady strength, you help others navigate their own obstacles. Together, you’ll build a culture that’s not just about surviving adversity, but about growing stronger because of it.
